summary: The game drops you right into space exploration and real world experience of how space missions work. We built a browser-based game that tackles what it's actually like to design a deep-space mission and deal with the fallout when things go sideways. Instead of basic survival tropes, you're wrestling with real aerospace trade-offs—like balancing a strict $3.0B budget and 10,000 kg mass limit between heavy hull armor or high-end science gear. If you skimp on armor, you're dealing with a brutal crash landing and intense repair work; if you over-insulate, you sacrifice crucial science instruments. Once you're on the surface, you're exploring -179°C methane lakes and cryovolcanic vents while managing finite data storage. And if you get stuck, our Socratic AI flight advisor won't just hand you the answers—it breaks down the physics and engineering realities so you have to make the hard calls yourself. It turns complex systems engineering into an engaging, high-stakes story that shows just how much sacrifice goes into true space exploration.
details: KHAGOL is a browser based space exploration and engineering game platform that makes learning about space more fun and interactive. It utilises real aerospace concepts to provide certain experiences like designing spacecraft, simulating space missions, exploring Mars with rovers, and surviving on Titan. Instead of just reading about space science, it helps users experiment with spacecraft designs, explore orbital mechanics, manage power systems and also understand how real space missions work. Our game runs directly in a web browser, so no installation is needed. Our aim is to make space engineering easier to understand and accessible to students, future engineers and possibly anyone who is curious about space. We built KHAGOL using Python, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS along with tools like Three.js for 3D models, E Charts for live data, GSAP for animations, and FastAPI for backend services. The thing that makes KHAGOL special is the way it combines real science with the excitement of a game. Users will get to design spacecraft, control Mars rovers, and explore distant worlds while learning how actual space missions work. While building it, we were focused on keeping the science realistic, while keeping the game easy to use and smooth across different devices.
dataRefs: 1. Project Details * Overview: What does it do or how does it work?  KHAGOL is an interactive, browser-based aerospace engineering and space mission simulation platform. It bridges the gap between complex astrodynamics and accessible STEM education.  The application works across four integrated modules:  Orbital Architect & 3D Spacecraft CAD: An interactive 3D workbench where players design spacecraft by mounting real-world components (optical imagers, Ka/X-band transceivers, ion thrusters, reaction wheels, solar arrays, and RTGs). Every design decision triggers authoritative aerospace margin calculations following AIAA S-120 standards (mass budgets, power balance, depth-of-discharge, link margins, and delta-v requirements). Authoritative Flight Simulator & Mission Operations: Propagates 365-day mission profiles across Earth, Lunar, Mars, Jovian, and Outer Solar System orbits, simulating solar eclipse cycles, telemetry downlink passes, battery degradation, thermal gradients, and anomaly mitigation. Mars Exploration Dual-Suite: A dual-mode simulation featuring a 50 kg orbital microsatellite designer and a Jezero Crater surface rover exploration game with battery energy economics, radio light-time delays, scientific rock drilling, and orbital relay coordination. Titan EVA Survival Game: A tactical atmospheric surface exploration game simulating cryo-methane lakes, radioisotope power dissipation, suit oxygen consumption, and scientific sample return. What benefits does it have? Active, Inquiry-Based STEM Learning: Replaces passive textbook formulas with real-time feedback—showing students exactly how mass margins affect launch costs or how orbital inclination impacts communication coverage. Zero-Install Accessibility: Runs directly in any modern web browser on laptops, desktops, and mobile devices with no specialized software or GPU requirements. Realistic Engineering Rigor: Incorporates real physical units ( 𝑘 𝑔 kg,  𝑊 W,  𝑑 𝐵 dB,  𝑚 / 𝑠 m/s), real orbital mechanics equations (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Vis-Viva, free-space path loss), and NASA margin principles rather than arbitrary arcade mechanics. What is the intended impact of the project?  KHAGOL aims to democratize space systems engineering for high school and university students, aspiring aerospace engineers, and space enthusiasts worldwide. By demystifying the trade-offs involved in space mission design—such as balancing payload scientific return against battery depth of discharge during solar eclipse—it inspires the next generation of space explorers, mission planners, and scientists.  What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use? Languages: Python 3.11, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3. Frontend Libraries & 3D Rendering: Three.js (r128), OrbitControls, Apache ECharts 5.4.3 (telemetry & power curves), GSAP 3.12.5 & ScrollTrigger (cinematic animations), Tailwind CSS, Canvas Confetti. Backend Architecture: FastAPI (ASGI REST server), Uvicorn, Pydantic v2 (boundary data validation). Physics & Engineering Algorithms: Custom client/server engines for AIAA S-120 mass/power margin auditing, orbital eclipse geometry, and RF link budget analysis. Deployment & Hosting: GitHub Pages (static distribution with client-side physics engines) and GitHub Actions. How is your project creative?  KHAGOL blends hard aerospace engineering standards with cinematic AAA game design. Rather than presenting dry technical spreadsheets, it immerses users inside a real-time Mission Operations Center with dynamic orbital lighting, telemetry feeds, audio-reactive radio beeps, and modular 3D spacecraft CAD visualization. Its creative "Connected Expedition" mechanics link orbital satellite passes directly with surface rovers on Mars, teaching the interdependency of space assets.  What factors did your team consider? Educational Accuracy vs. Playability: Balancing real orbital mechanics formulas with approachable, responsive UI feedback. Cross-Device Performance: Optimizing 3D geometry, limiting draw calls, and implementing frustum culling so the simulation achieves smooth 60 FPS performance on standard educational laptops. Zero-Dependency Portability: Designing the application to run both as a full-stack client-server architecture (run.bat / FastAPI) and as a zero-backend static web deployment on GitHub Pages. Accessibility & Usability: High-contrast dark themes inspired by NASA Open MCT, tooltips explaining technical acronyms, keyboard accessibility, and respect for prefers-reduced-motion. 2. Use of Super Intelligence (SI) *  (Check the appropriate boxes on your form for Code Generation, Data Modeling, and Image Generation. You can paste the following text into the description field):  Statement of SI Utilization: Super Intelligence (SI) and Large Language Model tools were utilized during development to accelerate software architecture, write repetitive boilerplate code, synthesize technical aerospace schemas, and generate project badge artwork.  Code & Data Modeling: SI tools were used to scaffold Pydantic schema validation models, formulate orbital math utilities (Keplerian two-body propagation, eclipse interval geometry), and build responsive UI layouts. All physics formulas, margin ratios, and component specifications were cross-referenced and verified against AIAA and NASA standards. Image Assets: The project badge (khagol_logo.png) was synthesized using browser-based AI image generation tools. No official NASA logos, meatball insignias, worm logos, flags, or protected mission identifiers were generated, modified, or infringed upon. All agency branding used throughout the project is original custom branding under the "KHAGOL" project banner. Audio: Audio cues are synthesized directly in real time using the native Web Audio API (AudioContext oscillator nodes) without pre-recorded copyrighted sound effects. 3.
